prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, in which magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms enabled frequency measurement at the 1e-18 level.

statement.case_for: I keep B046 as a single-part prize to Katori and Ye, and the first-round exchange has sharpened my reasons. The chair's novelty question has a one-sentence answer. The 2005 prize recognised the frequency comb, which is a ruler for optical frequencies. The 2012 prize recognised control of single quantum systems, ions and photons. The lattice clock is neither. Katori's magic-wavelength condition lets thousands of neutral atoms be held in a standing wave with the light shift cancelled on the clock transition, and that is what brings statistical power and small systematics together. The citation should say this explicitly so that it cannot be read as a third prize for the comb or for ion clocks. The maturity test I apply to any instrument is whether people who did not build it have reproduced the performance and then used it for something new. That has happened at JILA, RIKEN and Tokyo, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and others, with intercontinental comparisons and redshift resolved over millimetres. On the factual point the chair asked us to settle, I side with Kroll: the 2005 prize went to Glauber, Hall and Hansch, and Ye was in Hall's group but was not a laureate. Several of us, including me in round 1, carried the wrong impression from memory. That weakens the overlap argument, because the prior prize did not honour either proposed laureate, although the comb remains part of how clocks are read out. On attribution, Katori holds the concept and the first strontium lattice clock, and Ye holds the record accuracy and the many-body clock work. Two names is a defensible, plain citation. I do not think the SI redefinition of the second should count either way, because the science is already established.
statement.case_against: The best argument against is still the one raised by Danielsson, Eriksson and Olsson. B038 is a predicted and verified new state of matter, and B046 is a precision-measurement invention whose fundamental-physics output so far consists of limits and demonstrations, not discoveries. If the committee holds that the Prize should go first to discoveries, B038 wins on that axis. A second objection is attribution at the edges. Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and the ion-clock groups have real contributions, and a two-name prize leaves a visible gap that I cannot resolve from the material here. I also recall the priority history from memory and have not checked it against the primary papers. Finally, a clock prize adds to a line of metrology prizes in 2005 and 2012, and some will see that as crowding, even if the lattice invention is distinct.

responses.point: Kroll recalls that the 2005 laureates were Glauber, Hall and Hansch and that Ye, as Hall's postdoc, was not a laureate, which contradicts several of us. He also discloses his doctoral period in Hall's laboratory and possible recusal on B046.
responses.response: I think your recollection is correct and I withdraw the implication in my round-1 case against that Ye is tied to a prize he did not share. Please do not take that as a reason for the committee to relax on the comb: the readout still depends on it, and the citation should say plainly that the new element is lattice trapping at the magic wavelength. On your disclosure, I would ask you to declare it in the record and let the committee judge it. Your contribution on the physics of clock laser stabilisation is exactly what makes your view of the systematics worth having. If you decide to step back from the vote on B046, say so before the ballot so that the count is transparent. I also note that you were more open than I was to a third name. I still do not see how to add Lemonde or Ludlow without a clear argument that their contribution was decisive and not a very good follow-on.

responses.point: Olsson ranks B038 first as the cleanest prediction-then-experiment case, but says the credit is not clean (Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, 3D work), that the experimental side rests essentially on one group for the first observation, and that the committee should wait or reframe if it cannot be absolutely sure of the three names.
responses.response: I take your own test and apply it to B046 as well: can we be absolutely sure of the names? For Katori and Ye I believe we can, which is the main difference between the two leaders. The concept and first demonstration are Katori's, and the accuracy record and many-body clock work are Ye's. For B038 the gap on the HgTe proposal is, by your own account and Eriksson's, a real one, and the first observation rests on one group. I do not say B038 is lacking in physics. I am an experimentalist and I respect that Molenkamp's measurement was decisive. But your standard of being sure about who did the original work is met more cleanly by B046 today. If the committee leaned toward B038, I would want the citation limited to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall state and the gap stated openly in our rationale.

responses.point: Danielsson moved from WMAP to B038, arguing that the discovery of a new Z2 class of matter, confirmed in 2D and 3D by transport and ARPES, is the clearest 'clue from nature', and that a lattice-clock prize so far yields limits rather than findings.
responses.response: I agree that B038 is the cleaner discovery, and you could argue that the clock's fundamental-physics output is mostly limits so far. Where I differ is that I do not accept that an instrument that opens a new regime of measurement is a lesser category. Cosmic-ray antimatter and gamma-ray polarimetry are done with exactly this kind of detector advance, and the Prize has honoured such work when it changes what can be observed. A clock that resolves a gravitational redshift over a millimetre does that already. On the 2016 overlap you raised, I find your argument that time-reversal-invariant Z2 topology is distinct from the Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz work plausible, but I cannot judge it as a condensed-matter physicist would, and I note that Olsson, Lindroth and Kroll treat it as open. That leaves B038 with an overlap question and an attribution gap, and B046 with a novelty question that the magic-wavelength sentence answers. I have not changed my configuration because of this, but your case is why B038 is my first alternative.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B038 first as a verified chain from prediction to measurement, can speak from computational materials theory to how the idea changed the search for materials, and accepts the gap in HgTe and 3D attribution.
responses.response: In round 1 you said you would back B038 if B046 stalls. I take that seriously and I note that B046 is also on your list of alternatives. Your point that first-principles electronic-structure methods now routinely predict topological candidates is the strongest evidence that B038 has changed a field, and I could not have made that point. My concern remains the attribution. You identify the same gap as I do on the theory side. For the committee to prefer B038 on conceptual novelty alone it would have to accept that gap openly, and I would ask you whether a citation limited to the two-dimensional state really survives without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang. If your answer is that it does, I will weigh it, but I would still need a clear statement from the specialists that Kane and Mele are the right theory names for that state.

uncertainties: Whether specialists accept that a citation worded around magic-wavelength lattice trapping reads as distinct from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 prize on single quantum systems.
Whether Lemonde, Takamoto or Ludlow have a claim strong enough to alter the Katori and Ye pair. I judge not, but I cannot verify the priority history from the primary papers.
Whether the committee, applying the discovery-versus-instrument distinction, would put B038 first even after accepting its attribution gap and the 2016 overlap question.
Whether a two-part configuration (B046 with B038) is worth discussing, since the three-person cap makes it impossible with the full B038 trio plus Katori and Ye.
statement.conflict_note: I have no conflict on B046 or B038. B046 is atomic and metrology physics outside my own collaborations (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, XL-Calibur), and I have no stated tie to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp. For B025 I am professionally close to the neighbouring cosmic-ray and gamma-ray community around IceCube, with no personal tie to Halzen, and I hold that in mind because it is one of my alternatives. As chair I note Kroll's disclosure on B046 and ask that he state before the ballot whether he will recuse.
